In this task, you will evaluate whether each statement is supported by its corresponding citations. Note
that the system responses may appear very fluent and well-formed, but contain slight inaccuracies that are
not easy to discern at first glance. Pay close attention to the text.

You will be provided with a statement and its corresponding passage which the statement cites. It may be
helpful to ask yourself whether it is accurate to say “according to the citation ...” with the statement following this phrase. Be sure to check all of the information in the statement. You will be given three options:

• Full Support: All of the information in the statement is supported in the citation.
• Partial Support: Some parts of the information are supported in the citation, but other parts are missing.
• No Support: The citation does not support any part of the statement.

Please provide your response based on the information in the citation. If you are unsure, use your best
judgment. Respond as either “Full Support”, “Partial Support”, or “No Support” with no additional
information.
Statement: The in‑game economy forces players to weigh short‑term purchases against long‑term financial health, creating tension that blends action with strategy.
Citation: CS introduced an in-game economy system where players earn money based on their performance and the team's outcome in rounds. This money is then used to purchase weapons, equipment, and other utilities. The economy system transformed the pacing of matches, creating moments of tension and excitement. Players had to consider the long-term implications of their choices, blending action with strategy seamlessly.
Counter-Strike, in its various versions from 1.6 to Global Offensive, has maintained a dedicated player base for over two decades. Few games can boast such longevity. Its continuous appeal stems from both developer support and an ever-passionate player community. The evolution of CS versions reflects its commitment to staying current while respecting its core mechanics.
The success of Counter-Strike, particularly in terms of level design and balanced gameplay, has made it a topic of study in game design curricula. Aspiring game developers analyze the game's maps, mechanics, and pacing to understand what makes it so engaging. Courses emphasize the significance of map choke points, player flow, and risk-reward dynamics. These analyses prepare future developers to create balanced and enjoyable gaming experiences.
Counter-Strike tournaments are global events, with teams from North America, Europe, Asia, and other regions competing. The game's international appeal has played a role in bridging cultural gaps, fostering a global community of players and fans. Its reach has transcended borders, creating a universal language of gameplay. From Brazilian fans cheering their favorite teams to European powerhouses clashing in championships, CS unites players and spectators worldwide.
Counter-Strike's impact on the gaming industry is both wide and deep. It has not only defined competitive FPS gaming but has also set standards in game design, community involvement, and eSports. Its continued success stands as a testament to the title's timeless appeal and adaptability. From a mod to a global phenomenon, Counter-Strike's journey embodies the potential and dynamism of the gaming world.
The Elder Scrolls Series: A Pillar of Influence in Gaming
When discussions arise about the most influential role-playing games (RPGs), The Elder Scrolls series is invariably near the top of the list. Developed by Bethesda Game Studios, the series began with "The Elder Scrolls: Arena" in 1994 and has since expanded with main entries and spin-offs that have left profound marks on gaming's fabric. Its iconic presence has made it a staple for many gamers worldwide. The evolution and innovation within each title have cemented its status as a trendsetter in the gaming industry.
The Elder Scrolls games, especially from "Morrowind" onward, are best known for their vast, immersive open worlds. These settings are not merely backdrops but dynamic ecosystems where players can interact with every object, follow or diverge from the main narrative as they choose, and even influence the world around them. The sheer breadth and depth of exploration available have inspired countless developers. The series laid the groundwork for the open-world phenomenon that dominates today's gaming scene.

Question: What is the primary way players earn money in the in-game economy system of CS? Answer: Players earn money based on their performance and the team's outcome in rounds.

Question: What is the first game in The Elder Scrolls series? Answer: The Elder Scrolls: Arena

Question: Which game in The Elder Scrolls series is often considered the starting point for the iconic open-world experience? Answer: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind

</file>
